git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one rule in this case's list, "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else". Its other changes are outside the list: a new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, Before you finish step 1, the text of Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, and testing.md renamed to ex_unit.md with a new Assert with patterns sentence and example. The rewritten multi-line-argument rule finds no violation: the multi-line maps are return values (opus-1 lines 47-50 and 88-94, haiku-2 58-61, sonnet-2 29-32) or struct updates (haiku-1 45-49, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 62-66), not call arguments, and the literals passed to calls (haiku-1 line 33, sonnet-1 line 55, sonnet-2 line 47) fit on one line.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else". The clause-consistency sentences "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line. When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." are now "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line.", which decides the mixed functions here. Mixed functions: opus-1 parse_status!/2 (do: lines 119-121, blank line 122, block 123-125), haiku-1 add_completed/2 (block 42-50, blank 51, do: 52) and to_cents/1 (do: 62, blank 63, block 64-73), sonnet-1 add_completed/2 (block 58-67, blank 68, do: 69), sonnet-2 add_completed/2 (block 58-67, blank 68, do: 69); every block clause is set apart, so all are clean under the new sentence, and none would have failed the old one either (no function has most clauses as blocks with some on do:). Violating runs out of 5, per sentence: one-expression do: 0; several steps, case, with or comment under do: 0; block clause in a mixed function not set apart 0; do: body wrapped onto its own line, on a function or an if, 0 (every do: is on its head's line, as written and after formatting a copy, which changes only sonnet-2 line 30, a map field); the guard-wrap exception is not used. The only keyword if is sonnet-1 line 71 `if(DateTime.compare(a, b) == :lt, do: b, else: a)`, one line, held clean as the previous sweep held the same line.

Against the previous sweep's baseline: the with rule goes from violated in opus-1 to not exercised in all five (this opus-1 raises on a bad row instead of returning {:error, reason}).
